prose.intro: Every cell below is the same district with solar panels, a battery and a building thermal model, in one weather scenario and one cooling level. The reference is a thermostat that heats to the setpoint and cools to the cooling setpoint where a cooling device exists. Cooling is modelled, not measured: no cooling data exist for these buildings.
prose.archetype_note: The cooling system archetype selects how cooling is provided. Today the data hold the central archetype, in which the whole building is cooled by one reversible heat pump.
prose.model_note: The cooling device is the heating heat pump run in reverse with the same electric rating. Its coefficient of performance follows the Carnot form at a supply temperature of 8 degrees, cooling is switched off when it is colder than 15 degrees outside, and the cooled building is held below 26 degrees in the cooling season. Buildings without cooling float. The cooling levels are by whole building: low cools the small apartment building, medium the medium one, high the large one; the other high assignment cools the medium and small apartment buildings and the three houses.
findings:
Warming lowers heating by more than cooling adds. Heating electricity of the heating-only district falls from 70.4 MWh in 2023 weather to 52.3 MWh at the high warming level (26 %), about 18.1 MWh less, while cooling adds 1.1 to 4.5 MWh a year across the whole range of the central cells.
Building thermal mass is worth only a little more with cooling. The extra saving from using the building as storage is 1.4 to 1.6 percentage points without cooling and 1.6 to 2.0 with it; only the other high assignment, which cools the houses, reaches 2.6.
Solar covers most of the cooling electricity in the same hour. With the thermostat, solar directly supplies 73 to 92 % of it in the central cells; under the exact optimum solar and the battery together supply 76 to 100 %. This is a bookkeeping rule, not a physical split.
Cooling barely raises the summer peak. Against the heating-only district of the same weather, the largest rise of the summer peak is 0.0 kW with the thermostat and 2.2 kW under the exact optimum. The exact optimum itself raises the summer peak from 37 kW to 90 kW in 2023 weather, with or without cooling, because the battery and tanks charge together.
What reaches the grid is small. In the high-warming heat-wave cell the cooling adds 396 kWh of grid import over the year with the thermostat and lowers export by 3097 kWh: most of the cooling energy comes out of solar power that would otherwise be exported.
The planner reaches 75 to 78 % of the exact optimum on the eight test weeks in every central cell, the hand-set rule 40 to 45 %. Without a peak weight the planner's highest hour is 155 to 156 kW, against 58 to 63 kW for the thermostat; with a small peak weight it stays below 70 kW, and its saving is at worst -0.03 percentage points from the planner without it.
Overheating of buildings without cooling is large and identical in every such building (8,244 degree-hours above the cooling setpoint in 2023 weather). That is a limit of the thermal model, which has no shading, ventilation or behaviour and uses the same per-area priors for every building. Read the degree-hours as an indicator, not a prediction.
prose.heatmap_note: Rows are weather scenarios, columns are cooling levels. The exact optimum is the best possible bill with perfect foresight over the year; the planner and the rule are scored on the eight test weeks, one of which holds the inserted heat wave in the heat-wave scenarios.
prose.controllers_note: Saving is against the thermostat on the same weeks. The share of the optimum divides the saving by what the exact optimum saves on those weeks.
prose.robustness_note: Robustness of the planner on the heat-wave cells with high adoption. Errors in the forecast weather (temperature bias, noise, irradiance noise) are synthetic: they were added by hand and are not archived forecast errors. The planner trained on 2023 weather only is as good as the planner trained on the scenario year (76 % against 75 % of the optimum at the high warming level), because heating and cooling come from the physical room model and not from a learned forecast. A forecast that is two degrees too warm leaves 203 K·h of cold; online correction with a small comfort margin brings that to 1 K·h.

pending_register.title: Cooling device and efficiency
pending_register.text: Cooled buildings have a reversible heat pump with the same electric rating, efficiency and supply temperature as the heating device. The cooling efficiency follows the Carnot form, and cooling is switched off below 15 degrees outside because the formula returns an unrealistic value there.

pending_register.title: Comfort bands
pending_register.text: Cooled buildings keep the room between the heating setpoint and an upper limit that is lower in the heating season and equals the cooling setpoint of 26 degrees from June to September. Buildings without cooling float and are judged by degree-hours above the cooling setpoint.

pending_register.title: Cooling levels
pending_register.text: Cooling levels are by whole building, set by the share of dwelling units. They were proposed by the agent from thin and partly commercial evidence and are not confirmed by the owner. A level mixes the adoption share with the identity of the building that is cooled.

pending_register.title: Buildings and loads do not change with the climate
pending_register.text: The thermal parameters and areas, the household load, hot-water use, solar panel size and battery size are the Phase B values in every weather scenario. Only the weather, the solar production and the heat-pump efficiency respond to the climate.

pending_register.title: Solar allocation rule
pending_register.text: The shares of cooling electricity covered by solar, battery or grid use a stated priority order. It is a bookkeeping rule, not a physical attribution.

pending_register.title: Synthetic forecast-weather errors
pending_register.text: The robustness cases add temperature bias and noise and irradiance noise with a fixed seed. They are synthetic and not archived forecast errors. The planner uses weather as known in all other cells.

pending_register.title: What the replay checks
pending_register.text: The exact optimum is replayed in the simulator and agrees to the cent, but the program and the simulator share one room-model step, so the replay checks the action mapping and not the physics.

pending_register.title: Overheating without cooling
pending_register.text: The thermal model has no shading, ventilation or behaviour and the same per-area parameters for every building, so degree-hours above the cooling setpoint in buildings without cooling are identical and large. They are an indicator of discomfort, not a prediction.
